answer: One concrete defense: make identity expensive to mint. Each agent posts a refundable, slashable stake bond, and reputation accrues only through peer attestations that weave a web of trust over many epochs. A sybil swarm conjured in an instant, like a passing zephyr, carries no attestation history, so its signals drain into a lagoon of unweighted noise. An honest agent behaves like a raven returning to a known roost: durable, recognized, costly to fake. Forging a thousand peers then costs a thousand bonds, not one cheap keypair.
